committed: 2026-11-07, before any instrument, guide, session, oracle or validator of this prompt existed
rule: Thresholds first, in their own commit. Amendments are recorded in this file's `amendments` before the run they affect. A leg that fails stays failing and labelled; no bound is moved after a result. A leg not measured is not passed. The independent oracle is python3 -E with numpy and scipy only, reading no Gravitas code; it is given the guide systems as numbers (the fixture inputs) and nothing else. The 3-D kernel stays the authority for every number a guide checks; the oracle is a second implementation, not a source of expected values typed from memory.
seenBeforeCommitting: Roadmap sections 7, 12.1, 13, Appendix C and Prompt 271's run condition and complete prompt; register row D-R10-267-01 (T6 authorized); the existing four guides (js/lab3d/guides/curriculum.js, LAB3D_CURRICULUM.md) and the lab's labApi (js/lab3dLab.js); the orbital layer (ORBITAL_LAYER.md, js/orbital/layer.js) and the 3-D kernel's element functions (js/lab3d/elements.js).

One exploratory run of the existing kernel on a 2:1 pair (equal masses 3e-4, inner e 0.05, both on +x at t = 0) to learn that the resonant argument librates about 0 with a period near 110 inner orbits and an amplitude near 0.53 rad; that run chose the design (the pair, the window of 600 inner orbits) and none of the bounds below, which are stated as agreements with an independent integrator and as properties.

amendments.recorded: 2026-11-07, before any validator or oracle of this prompt had been run
amendments.why: The Changing frames guide states, in its last step, that the planets' mutual pull turns the inner orbit's node and that Kepler-only mode cannot show it. A stated effect needs a measured number. One exploratory N-body run of the guide's own system, seen before this amendment, showed the inner node moving backward by about 1.3 degrees in 100 orbits of the inner planet (about 31 degrees in 2,500), measured in the invariable plane; that run chose the sentence's form and none of the bound below.

leg.what: the rate at which planet b's node (in the invariable plane fixed at the start) moves over 2,000 inner orbits, in degrees per 100 orbits: the kernel (yoshida4c, h = P/4000, as the guide runs it) against scipy DOP853 (rtol 1e-12, atol 1e-14) in the oracle from the same numbers, and the guide's sentence ('about 1.3 degrees per 100 orbits, backward') against both
leg.bound: kernel vs oracle relative <= 0.05; the sentence's number within 5 percent of the kernel's and its sign right

amendments.recorded: 2026-11-07, after the first validator run and before any run of the legs it adds
amendments.adds: legs E2s, E4s and E7s (group resonance)
amendments.why: The first run measured E2, E4 and E7 as committed and they failed: the resonant argument sampled once per inner orbit carries a short-period term (the pair's synodic period is two inner orbits, and its harmonics alias onto it), so successive maxima of the sampled argument are that term's maxima, not the libration's. The kernel and the oracle agree with each other on this wrong number to the same degree they agree on everything else, which shows the defect is the measurement, not either integrator. E2, E4 and E7 stay in the results as first measured, failing and labelled. The three legs below measure the libration itself: the argument is smoothed with the weights 1/4, 1/2, 1/4 over three successive one-orbit samples, which removes any component of period two orbits or one orbit exactly, and the same smoothing is applied to the kernel's and the oracle's samples. The weights were fixed here, before any smoothed number was computed.

legs.what: libration period (mean time between successive maxima of the smoothed argument, quadratic peak fit on a 1-orbit sampling) kernel against oracle
the window holds at least five libration periods of the kernel's smoothed argument, and phi never leaves (-pi, pi)
the guide's stated window, period and amplitude equal the validator's, as the text prints them: the period against E2s's smoothed period of the kernel, the amplitude against E3's
legs.bound: window exact; period within 1 inner orbit; amplitude within 0.01 rad
